findings.english_quote: “Renewed our life” follows the printed form compared with Latin Vulgata and Palatina; the apparatus reports an Athos form meaning “renewed” with different grammar. Renewing the spirit and renewing life remain distinct expressions.
findings.issue: The supplied apparatus transcription reports ἀνένευσε A, not another grammatical form straightforwardly meaning “renewed.” As written, ἀνένευσε belongs to ἀνανεύω, associated with nodding or a gesture of refusal. The note therefore mischaracterizes the reported alternative by asserting semantic agreement and merely different grammar. The supplied evidence does not establish that this is an orthographic corruption intended to mean “renewed.” This does not invalidate the selected working reading ἀνενέωσε.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain “renewed our life” in the main text. Revise the note to disclose the exact reported form and the interpretive limit, for example: “The printed working text reads ἀνενέωσε, ‘renewed,’ with Latin Vulgata and Palatina cited in the apparatus. The apparatus reports Athos ἀνένευσε, a different form whose intended sense here is uncertain; the supplied report does not establish it as another grammatical form meaning ‘renewed.’ Renewing the spirit and renewing life remain distinct expressions.” Any stronger explanation of the Athos form requires additional attributed evidence. The proposed note requires fresh review.

findings.english_quote: “Renewed our life” follows the printed form compared with Latin Vulgata and Palatina; the apparatus reports an Athos form meaning “renewed” with different grammar. Renewing the spirit and renewing life remain distinct expressions.
findings.issue: Independently checked against the selected Greek and supplied apparatus, this note makes the same unsupported characterization: the reported Athos reading is ἀνένευσε, not an established same-meaning grammatical variant of ἀνενέωσε. Its written form belongs to ἀνανεύω, associated with nodding or a gesture of refusal. Neither the supplied transcription nor the comparison reports establish that it was intended as an orthographic corruption meaning “renewed.” The simplified main text correctly retains the working reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep “he renewed our life.” Replace the inaccurate variant description with an explicit report, for example: “The working text reads ‘renewed.’ Its apparatus cites Latin Vulgata and Palatina and reports Athos ἀνένευσε, a different Greek form whose intended meaning here is uncertain. The supplied evidence does not establish that this form also means ‘renewed.’ The source separately describes renewal of our spirit and our life.” Any stronger account needs additional attributed evidence, and this proposed replacement requires fresh review.

summary: Both editions require revision of note c’s characterization of the reported Athos alternative. Otherwise, clause-by-clause review found no concrete fidelity defect in either main text: the conditions, negations, necessity, speakers, distinct renewals, and difficult assertions are preserved. Repentance wording follows current policy, and the bracketed supplements are disclosed. This review evaluates the supplied working source and attributed reports; it does not authenticate manuscript images or certify an exhaustive collation.
